findings.description: Critical: Per-mode agents.yaml isolation overrides cannot take effect on the reachable-router path under the planned precedence. Spec and plan say router wins when reachable, then get_agent_isolation(), then none; the plan only teaches get_agent_isolation(agent_type, dispatch_mode?) to honor cli.dispatch_modes.<mode>.isolation. Current producers always emit entry-level isolation: resolver.py builds RoutingAssignment with lane.get("isolation") or "none", and routing_fallback.py does the same with entry.get("isolation"). After dg-05 as scoped, a review/alternative override is ignored whenever a routing decision exists, so the acceptance outcome that an (agent_type, dispatch_mode) pair resolves with per-mode overrides fails on the primary path.
findings.resolution: Require emission sites owned by dg-05 (coordinator lane assignment and skills local-static fallback) to attach isolation via the same (agent_type, dispatch_mode) resolution helper before the decision is treated as the router rung. Keep dg-06 limited to carrying/obeying that decision; do not leave mode-aware emission only on the fallback get_agent_isolation rung.

findings.description: Critical: The plan consolidates vocabulary into one isolation_contract module imported by agents_config and model_routing, but leaves the live third copy in skills/coordination-bridge/scripts/routing_fallback.py (_ISOLATION_VALUES = frozenset({"none", "worktree", "sandbox"})). That module intentionally re-validates routing.yaml without importing agent-coordinator. Unless the shared module is dependency-neutral and skills-importable, and routing_fallback switches to it, the ADDED requirement that the vocabulary is defined once and referenced by producer and consumer is already false on the coordinator-unreachable path dg-05 claims to pin.
findings.resolution: Place isolation_contract where both agent-coordinator and skills can import it without a coordinator dependency (skills/shared or an equivalent tiny shared package). Make routing_fallback.py import VALID_ISOLATION_MODES/validation from that module; treat updating this copy as in-scope for dg-05, not dg-06.

findings.description: Critical: Proposed unreachable/silent wording (“use fallback config then none”) collides with dg-04’s already-shipped meaning of fallback. routing.yaml fallback.isolation_order is only a deterministic lane tie-break among configured values while the coordinator is unreachable (implement-the-task-router design D8/D9); it is explicitly not isolation-strength precedence. The dg-05 ladder in specs/vendor-dispatch/spec.md is router → agents.yaml via get_agent_isolation() → none. Implementing “fallback config” as isolation_order would either invent a fourth rung or reinterpret dg-04 fallback as enforcement policy.
findings.resolution: Name the ladder rungs exactly: routing decision when present; else get_agent_isolation(agent_type, dispatch_mode); else none. State that routing.yaml fallback.isolation_order remains a dg-04 local-static sort key only and is out of band for effective-isolation resolution.
findings.existing_code:
The fallback table's order is only a deterministic choice among the lane's exact
configured values while the coordinator is unreachable. It is not an isolation-strength
precedence or enforcement policy.

findings.description: Critical: “Router reachable but silent” is unspecified against post-dg-04 behavior. PolicyEvaluation.isolation may be None when no rule constrains isolation, but both coordinator and local-static assignment paths still always populate assignment.isolation from the lane (defaulting with or "none"). Without defining silence as “no routing decision / missing isolation field on the decision object” versus “policy did not constrain isolation,” implementers can treat ordinary lane-filled decisions as silent and incorrectly fall through to agents.yaml, or never hit the agents.yaml rung at all.
findings.resolution: Add scenarios that distinguish (1) decision present with isolation set, (2) decision absent/unreachable, (3) decision present but isolation field missing/null, and (4) invalid isolation value. Reject (4); do not treat policy-dimension None alone as router silence after an assignment has been built.

findings.description: Critical: Enabling cli.dispatch_modes.<mode>.isolation requires more than ModeConfig.args growth. AGENTS_SCHEMA currently sets additionalProperties: false on each dispatch mode object and lists only args/async/poll, so a per-mode isolation key fails agents.yaml validation today. The configured-lane dump path also serializes only args/async/poll and would drop a parsed mode isolation on round-trip. Plan/tasks do not call out these schema and serialization updates, so the feature is incompatible with the current loader/exporter even if the dataclass changes.
findings.resolution: Explicitly update AGENTS_SCHEMA mode properties to allow isolation enum values; parse into ModeConfig; emit isolation in the agents dump when set; add load-reject tests for unknown mode isolation values and round-trip tests for a per-mode override.

findings.description: Critical: Concrete contract tests are missing from the plan artifacts. tasks.md is still a generic scaffold, and neither proposal nor spec lists deterministic coverage for: shared-module single-definition imports from agent-coordinator and skills; precedence source recording (router vs agents.yaml vs none); unrecognized value rejection vs unreachable fallback; ModeConfig.isolation parse/default; get_agent_isolation(agent_type, dispatch_mode) override vs entry-level fallback; and local-static using mode-aware isolation. Without those pins, dg-05 can merge as a type alias shuffle while the ladder and per-mode behavior remain unproven.
findings.resolution: Replace scaffold tasks with test-first packages covering the cases above, including skills/tests/coordination-bridge coverage so the unreachable path cannot keep a private vocabulary or ignore per-mode overrides.

findings.description: Critical: Scope that “excludes dg-06 consumer dispatch wiring” is being used too broadly if it also skips emission/validation sites that dg-04 already made responsible for isolation data. dg-04 design D9 assigns per-mode overrides and the precedence ladder to dg-05, while dg-06 only owns calling routing before dispatch_fn. Leaving resolver/local-static entry-level emission and the skills vocabulary copy untouched means dg-05 cannot satisfy its own producer/consumer and (agent_type, dispatch_mode) acceptance outcomes, and pushes contract work into the wrong later item.
findings.resolution: Keep dg-06/dg-07 exclusions limited to orchestrator dispatch context wiring and OS sandbox enforcement. In dg-05 scope: shared contract module, schema/types, mode-aware helpers, producer emission aligned to (agent_type, dispatch_mode), and skills local-static vocabulary/resolution alignment.

findings.description: FYI: Sibling change add-sandboxed-harness-execution / docs/proposals/sandboxed-harness-execution.md explicitly asks dg-05 to admit container into the pinned isolation vocabulary while the contract is open, and its draft schemas already enum none|worktree|sandbox|container. The proposed dg-05 plan freezes {none, worktree, sandbox}. Landing dg-05 without a recorded decision forces a later vocabulary reopen or leaves the sibling proposal inconsistent with the pinned contract.
findings.resolution: Human decision before implementation: either keep the three-value vocabulary and require the sandbox-harness proposal to stop depending on dg-05 for container, or amend pin-isolation-contract now to admit container as a closed value with no backend obligation in dg-05.
